engagement_background.objective: Create measurable cost savings by strategically sourcing approximately $19 M of spend across key clinical, technology and indirect categories, while establishing stronger procurement processes and controls to support Advantia Health’s broader value-creation goals.
engagement_background.scope_summary: The project covers 10 spend categories identified via AP/P-card analysis (Employee Benefits, Medical Devices-IUDs, Diagnostic Devices & Services, Billing Systems/RCM, Medical Supplies, Medical Equipment, Telecom – Data & Voice, Electronic Payment Processing, Data Center/Cloud Hosting, Office Supplies), totaling about $18.98 M in spend. Employee Benefits is an optional later wave, and categories may be dropped if found non-addressable; the engagement also includes a high-level review of procurement processes/controls.
constraints_challenges: Fragmented, clinic-level purchasing spread across Advantia (Mid-Atlantic) and Heartland business units, creating supplier and data fragmentation.
Lack of dedicated strategic procurement resources; client staff have limited availability for sourcing activities.
Line-item usage and contract data are not centrally stored, requiring repeated requests to suppliers—some of whom do not respond for 6+ weeks.
Savings in several categories depend on behavior changes or standardization (e.g., enforcing 5-unit IUD order minimums, adopting a single sonography equipment manufacturer).
Tight 4–6-month timeline (with a later Benefits wave) and a minimum savings guarantee of ~$450-500 K place schedule and results pressure on the project.
Strong incumbent supplier relationships with clinical staff could generate resistance to switching vendors or terms.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Treasury/AP and P-card transaction data from two separate systems were available for October 2020–September 2021; most contract files and detailed usage data had to be requested individually from suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Supplier naming inconsistencies, limited item descriptions, missing line-level volumes, and absence of a central contract repository complicated spend categorization and baseline creation.
